For each $a$, let $\mathsf{Large}_a=\{i : (a,i)\in \mathsf{Large}\}$ and define \[ Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Large}_a} \lvert v_{a,i} \rangle\langle v_{a,i} \rvert. \] Then $\sum_a \mathrm{rank}(Q_a)=|\mathsf{Large}| \leq d$, and $Q_a \leq R_a$ for every $a$, so \[ Q = \sum_a Q_a \leq \sum_a R_a = R \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I. \] Also, \[ R_a-Q_a = \sum_{i \in \mathsf{Small}_a} \lvert v_{a,i} \rangle\langle v_{a,i} \rvert \] is a projector, hence \[ \sum_a \Vert (R_a-Q_a)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle\Vert^2 = \sum_{(a,i)\in\mathsf{Small}} o_{a,i} \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \] by \ref{eq:small-overlaps}. Therefore $R_a \otimes I \approx_{4\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \otimes I$. Combining this with \ref{lem:projective-non-measurement} and the triangle inequality for $\approx_\delta$ gives \[ A_a \otimes I \approx_{12\sqrt{\zeta}} Q_a \otimes I. \]

nodes.name: Completeness of~$Q$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \langle \psi \rvert Q \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq 1 - 11 \zeta^{1/4}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:Q-completeness

nodes.statement: Since each $Q_a$ is projective, \begin{equation} \langle \psi \rvert Q \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \approx_{5\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a \cdot A_a)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} By Cauchy--Schwarz, \[ \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \leq 1+2\sqrt{\zeta} \quad\text{and}\quad \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a-A_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \leq 12\sqrt{\zeta} \] from \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}. A second Cauchy--Schwarz estimate yields \begin{equation} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a \cdot A_a)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \approx_{4\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (A_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} Combining \ref{eq:Q-for-an-A} and \ref{eq:another-Q-for-A} with \ref{eq:A-looks-projective} gives \[ \langle \psi \rvert Q \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert A_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - 2\zeta - 9\zeta^{1/4} = 1 - 11\zeta^{1/4}, \] since $\zeta \leq \zeta^{1/4}$ under \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta}.

nodes.name: Completeness of~$\sqrt{Q}$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \langle \psi \rvert \sqrt{Q} \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq 1 - 12 \zeta^{1/4}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:sqrt-Q-completeness

nodes.statement:
Diagonalize $Q=\sum_i 
u_i \lvert u_i angle\langle u_i vert$. Because $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by ef{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, each $
u_i$ is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$. Therefore \[ \sqrt{Q} = \sum_i \sqrt{
u_i}\lvert u_i angle\langle u_i vert \geq  rac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} Q. \] The scalar estimate \[  rac{1}{\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{\zeta}}} \geq 1-\sqrt{\zeta} \] gives $\sqrt{Q} \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})Q$. Hence ef{lem:Q-completeness} implies \[ \langle \psi vert \sqrt{Q} \otimes I \lvert \psi angle \geq (1-\sqrt{\zeta})(1-11\zeta^{1/4}) \geq 1-12\zeta^{1/4}. \]

nodes.name: $Q$ is almost projective
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \sum_a (Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a) \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta} \cdot I. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:q-almost-projective

nodes.statement: Since $Q \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, \begin{align*} \sum_a Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a & \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) \sum_a Q_a \cdot I \cdot Q_a - \sum_a Q_a \\ & = (1+2\sqrt{\zeta})Q - Q \\ & = 2\sqrt{\zeta}\,Q \\ & \leq 2\sqrt{\zeta}(1+2\sqrt{\zeta})I \\ & \leq 4\sqrt{\zeta}\,I, \end{align*} using \ref{eq:assumption-on-zeta} in the last step.

nodes.name: Matrix decomposition of~$Q_a$
nodes.statement: For each $a$, let \[ m_a = \mathrm{rank}(Q_a), \] and let $\lvert v_{a,1} \rangle,\ldots,\lvert v_{a,m_a} \rangle$ be an orthonormal basis for the range of $Q_a$, so that \[ Q_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \lvert v_{a,i} \rangle\langle v_{a,i} \rvert. \] Let \[ m = \sum_a m_a, \] and let $\{\lvert a,i \rangle\}$ be an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^m$, indexed by all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$. For each $a$, define \[ X_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \lvert a,i \rangle\langle v_{a,i} \rvert, \qquad T_a = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \lvert a,i \rangle\langle a,i \rvert, \] and define \begin{equation} X = \sum_a X_a = \sum_a \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \lvert a,i \rangle\langle v_{a,i} \rvert. \end{equation} Let $T = \{T_a\}$. Then $T$ is a projective measurement on $\mathbb{C}^m$.
nodes.label: def:matrix-decomposition-Q

nodes.statement: Choose an orthonormal basis of the range of each projector \(Q_a\). The rank-one expansion gives the displayed decomposition, and the orthogonality of the labelled basis vectors makes the family \(T\) a projective measurement.

nodes.name: SVD of~$X$
nodes.statement: The paper presents this step by choosing a singular value decomposition \[ X = U \cdot \Sigma_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] The formalization has two closely related auxiliary declarations. The reduced datum records the downstream consequences of the choice: the matrices $X$ and $\widehat X$, the identities $X^\dagger X=Q$, $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$, and $X^\dagger\widehat X=\sqrt Q$, together with the $Q_a=X^\dagger T_aX$ restatement. The rectangular-SVD lemmas take explicit matrices $U,V,\Sigma,I_{m\times d}$ and derive the two stored $\widehat X$ identities from the matrix calculation below.
nodes.label: def:svd-of-X

nodes.statement: Apply the finite-dimensional singular value decomposition to \(X\) and record exactly the consequences used later: the identities for \(X^\dagger X\), \(\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger\), \(X^\dagger\widehat X\), and the restatement of the \(Q_a\)'s. The unitary-group constructors are the same rectangular-SVD calculation, with the square factors taken as elements of the relevant unitary groups rather than as matrices accompanied by separate unitarity equations. In the sigma-range specialization, the auxiliary row space is the lifted finite-enumeration carrier associated to the ranks of the \(Q_a\)'s, which is definitionally the carrier of the canonical sigma-range \(Q\)-layer.

nodes.name: Formalization support for orthogonal projector families
nodes.statement: If the family $\{Q_a\}$ were a projective measurement, then the vectors $\lvert v_{a,i} \rangle$, over all $a$ and all $1 \leq i \leq m_a$, would be orthonormal. Then \eqref{eq:looks-like-singular-value-decomposition} would already be a singular value decomposition of $X$, with $\Sigma = I_{m \times d}$. Equivalently, \[ X = U \cdot I_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] This motivates replacing $\Sigma$ by $I$ in the definition of $\widehat X$ and $P$.
nodes.label: rem:motivation-for-P

nodes.name: Definition of~$P$
nodes.statement: The paper defines \[ \widehat{X} = U \cdot I_{m \times d} \cdot V^\dagger. \] We take $\widehat X$ to be the reduced matrix supplied by the stored datum. For each $a$, define \[ \widehat{X}_a = T_a \cdot \widehat{X}, \qquad P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a. \]
nodes.label: def:projective-P

nodes.statement: The definition is the formal \(Q/X/\widehat X/P\) construction: once \(\widehat X\) is chosen from the stored singular-value data, each \(P_a\) is defined as the positive operator \(\widehat X_a^\dagger\widehat X_a\).
For each $a$, \[ X_a = T_a \cdot X. \]
nodes.label: lem:xa-t

nodes.statement: Multiply the definition of $X$ by $T_a$ on the left and use that $T_a$ selects exactly the basis vectors $\lvert a,i \rangle$: \[ T_a \cdot X = \Big(\sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \lvert a,i \rangle\langle a,i \rvert\Big) \Big(\sum_b \sum_{j=1}^{m_b} \lvert b,j \rangle\langle v_{b,j} \rvert\Big) = \sum_{i=1}^{m_a} \lvert a,i \rangle\langle v_{a,i} \rvert = X_a. \]

nodes.name: $Q_a$ restated
nodes.statement: For each $a$, \begin{equation*} Q_a = X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:qa-restated

nodes.statement: The identity $X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$ follows by expanding the basis sums. The remaining equalities come from \ref{lem:xa-t} and the projectivity of $T$: \[ X_a^\dagger \cdot X_a = (X^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot X) = X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = X_a^\dagger \cdot X. \]

nodes.name: $X$ squared
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} X^\dagger \cdot X = Q. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:X-squared

nodes.statement: Use that $T$ is a measurement and then \ref{lem:qa-restated}: \[ X^\dagger \cdot X = \sum_a X^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot X = \sum_a Q_a = Q. \] The additional paper identities involving $U,V,\Sigma$ are the usual SVD computations. The Lean development also records the spectral calculation which will identify the mixed positive-Gram-image product with $\sqrt Q$: the positive eigenvalues give the nonzero columns, while the zero eigenspace has zero coefficient in the square-root expansion and is killed by $X$. The conjugate right-eigenvector rows over the positive spectrum are also orthonormal. Equivalently, any row-space vector orthogonal to the positive Gram images is killed by $X^\dagger$.
For each $a$, \begin{equation*} X_a^\dagger \cdot (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2 \cdot X_a = Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a - Q_a. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression

nodes.statement: Expand the square and apply \ref{lem:X-squared} and \ref{lem:qa-restated} term by term: \[ X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a = Q_a \cdot Q \cdot Q_a, \] while \[ X_a^\dagger (X \cdot X^\dagger) X_a = (X_a^\dagger \cdot X)(X^\dagger \cdot X_a) = Q_a \cdot Q_a = Q_a, \] and $X_a^\dagger I_{m \times m} X_a = X_a^\dagger X_a = Q_a$. Substituting these identities into \[ (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2 = X \cdot X^\dagger \cdot X \cdot X^\dagger - 2X \cdot X^\dagger + I_{m \times m} \] gives the claim.

nodes.name: $P_a$ restated
nodes.statement: For each $a$, \begin{equation*} P_a = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:pa-restated

nodes.statement: Since $T$ is projective, \[ P_a = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}_a = (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a)(T_a \cdot \widehat{X}) = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} = \widehat{X}_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}. \]

nodes.name: $\widehat{X}$ squared
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \widehat{X} \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = I_{m \times m}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:X-hat-squared

nodes.statement: The paper proves this by multiplying out $\widehat{X}=U\cdot I_{m\times d}\cdot V^\dagger$ and using the unitarity of $U$ and $V$. In Lean, the dimension hypothesis $m\leq d$ already gives a rectangular matrix with orthonormal rows on the sigma auxiliary space; the chosen matrix \texttt{sigmaFinXHatCoisometry} and its specification record this existence result as a hypothesis for the future construction. The formal lemma \texttt{orthonormal\_normalized\_image\_of\_adjoint\_comp\_eigenvectors} records the singular-vector normalization calculation, while \texttt{normalized\_matrix\_image\_rows\_mul\_conjTranspose} combines the corresponding row-coisometry identity, and \texttt{positive\_gram\_spectrum\_image\_rows\_transpose\_mixed} records the adjoint action $X^\dagger(\lambda^{-1/2}Xv)=\lambda^{1/2}v$ on the positive spectral part of the Gram operator. The formal lemma \texttt{exists\_unitaryGroup\_with\_positive\_gram\_spectrum\_rows} records the next finite-dimensional step: after choosing distinct row positions for the positive spectrum, these normalized image rows extend to a square unitary group element on the row space. The companion lemma \texttt{exists\_rectangular\_coisometry\_extending\_orthonormal\_rows} records the analogous rectangular completion for prescribed right rows when the dimension bound permits it. The formal lemma \texttt{unitaryGroup\_mul\_rectangular\_coisometry} and its right-multiplication companion \texttt{rectangular\_coisometry\_mul\_conjTranspose\_unitaryGroup} record the two unitary-preservation steps in the paper's multiplication. The formal lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_coisometry\_unitaryGroup} applies these preservation steps to the rectangular-SVD expression. The unconditional positive-Gram route is \texttt{exists\_xHat\_of\_sigmaFinRangeEmbedding\_positiveGram}, which constructs $\widehat X$ from the rank-reduction witness and proves $\widehat X\widehat X^\dagger=I$ together with the mixed square-root identity below.

nodes.name: $X$ times $\widehat{X}$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} X \cdot \widehat{X}^\dagger = U \cdot \Sigma_{m \times m} \cdot U^\dagger, \quad X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} = \sqrt{Q}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:X-times-X-hat

nodes.statement: The paper obtains this from the SVD formula for $X$ and the definition of $\widehat X$. In Lean, the unconditional QXP data first proves that $X\widehat X^\dagger$ is Hermitian and positive. The formal lemma \texttt{x\_mul\_xHat\_adjoint\_spectral\_theorem} then applies Mathlib's spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, giving the displayed $U\Sigma U^\dagger$ form with the Mathlib eigenvector unitary and the diagonal matrix of real eigenvalues. The auxiliary lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_x\_mul\_xHat\_conjTranspose\_raw} records the same calculation under explicit rectangular-SVD data, where the middle factor \(S I_{m\times d}^\dagger\) is the formal square matrix \(\Sigma_{m\times m}\). The formal lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_xHat\_mixed\_of\_sqrtQ\_unitaryGroup} records the second matrix calculation in the form whose square-root target is the operator $Q$ supplied by the QXP construction. The formal lemma \texttt{rectangularSvd\_middle\_eq\_sqrt\_of\_square} records the spectral step: a positive middle factor whose square is $Q$ is the positive square root of $Q$. The reduced datum then records this mixed-product identity as a primitive consequence, which is exactly the part needed in \ref{lem:squared-difference} and \ref{lem:P-Q-approx}.

nodes.name: Lean status for the QXP algebra
nodes.statement: The Lean declarations linked in Lemmas~\ref{lem:X-squared}, \ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, and~\ref{lem:X-times-X-hat} expose the corresponding matrix identities as construction theorems. These declarations prove the identities from the \(Q\)-layer, the sigma-range realization, and the positive-Gram spectral construction, with the rectangular-SVD calculation retained as an auxiliary comparison. Thus the local \(X/\widehat X/P\) algebra is formalized; the remaining chapter-level work is to compose this construction with the preceding orthonormalization step from the paper hypotheses.
nodes.label: rem:qxp-layer-lean-status

nodes.name: Squared difference
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} (X - \widehat{X}) \cdot (X - \widehat{X})^\dagger \leq (X \cdot X^\dagger - I_{m \times m})^2. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:squared-difference

nodes.statement: The paper diagonalizes the positive operator $X\widehat X^\dagger$ using the SVD notation. The formal proof avoids storing that SVD explicitly: set $Y=X\widehat X^\dagger$. The primitive identities imply that $Y$ is hermitian, nonnegative, and satisfies $Y^2=XX^\dagger$. Hence $(X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger=(Y-I)^2$, and positivity of $Y$ gives $(Y-I)^2\leq(Y^2-I)^2=(XX^\dagger-I)^2$.

nodes.name: Projectivity of~$P$
nodes.statement: $P = \{P_a\}$ forms a projective sub-measurement.
nodes.label: lem:P-projectivity

nodes.statement: For outcomes $a,b$, \begin{align*} P_a \cdot P_b & = (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X}) (\widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X}) \\ & = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot I_{m \times m} \cdot T_b \cdot \widehat{X} \\ & = \widehat{X}^\dagger \cdot T_a \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot \mathbf{1}\!\left[[\right]a=b] \\ & = P_a \cdot \mathbf{1}\!\left[[\right]a=b], \end{align*} where the second line uses \ref{lem:X-hat-squared}, the third uses that $T$ is projective, and the last uses \ref{lem:pa-restated}. Summing over $a$ shows $\sum_a P_a \leq I$, so $P$ is a projective sub-measurement. The formalization also records the sharper identity \[ \sum_a P_a=\widehat X^\dagger\widehat X, \] and the resulting total-domination estimates used later in the monotone-total self-improvement route.

nodes.name: $P$ is close to~$Q$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} Q_a \otimes I \approx_{30\zeta^{1/4}} P_a \otimes I. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:P-Q-approx

nodes.statement: The formal proof follows this argument directly from the primitive $X$, $\widehat X$, and $P$ identities; the $30\zeta^{1/4}$ estimate is derived here rather than stored as part of the reduced datum. The unitary-group rectangular-SVD lemma combines the same estimate with the positive-square identification of the middle factor from \ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}; the square unitary factors are again carried as elements of the relevant unitary groups. The positive-Gram sigma-space lemma also records the coisometry \(X X^\dagger=I\) for the original sigma embedding when the projective \(Q\)-family is subnormalized; this is the construction-level hypothesis later used to obtain the QXP-internal fresh-outcome comparison \(Q_{\mathrm{none}} \leq P_{\mathrm{none}}\). An additional source-to-\(Q\) comparison is still needed for source-facing residual domination. The quantity to bound is \begin{equation} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a-P_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \langle \psi \rvert Q \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle + \langle \psi \rvert P \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert Q_aP_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert P_aQ_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle, \end{equation} using the projectivity of $Q$ and $P$. The first term is at most $1+2\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:projective-low-rank-sum}, and the second is at most $1$ because $P$ is a sub-measurement. For the last two terms, \begin{equation} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert Q_aP_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle + \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert P_aQ_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = 2 \cdot \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \langle \psi \rvert Q_aP_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle\Big). \end{equation} By \ref{lem:qa-restated}, \[ \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert Q_aP_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \] The main estimate is \begin{equation} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (X_a^\dagger \cdot X \cdot P_a)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \approx_{2\zeta^{1/4}} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} This follows by Cauchy--Schwarz: \[ \Big|\sum_a \langle \psi \rvert ((X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)) \otimes I)\cdot(P_a \otimes I)\lvert \psi \rangle\Big| \] is bounded by the square root of \[ \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert \big(X_a^\dagger \cdot (X-\widehat X)(X-\widehat X)^\dagger \cdot X_a\big)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle, \] times the square root of $\sum_a \langle \psi \rvert(P_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \leq 1$. The first factor is at most $4\sqrt{\zeta}$ by \ref{lem:squared-difference}, \ref{lem:X-expression-to-Q-expression}, and \ref{lem:q-almost-projective}, so the total error is at most $2\zeta^{1/4}$. The right-hand side of \ref{eq:add-a-hat} is real, because \[ \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (X_a^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X} \cdot P_a)\otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \langle \psi \rvert (X^\dagger \cdot \widehat{X}) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \langle \psi \rvert \sqrt{Q} \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle, \] where the first equality uses \ref{lem:xa-t}, \ref{lem:pa-restated}, and \ref{lem:X-hat-squared} and that $T$ is a measurement, and the second uses \ref{lem:X-times-X-hat}. Hence \ref{lem:sqrt-Q-completeness} and \ref{eq:add-a-hat} imply \[ \mathfrak{R}\Big(\sum_a \langle \psi \rvert Q_aP_a \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle\Big) \geq 1-14\zeta^{1/4}. \] Substituting this into \ref{eq:complex-conjugates} and then into \ref{eq:P-Q-thing-to-bound} gives \[ \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert (Q_a-P_a)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \leq (1+2\sqrt{\zeta}) + 1 - 2(1-14\zeta^{1/4}) = 2\sqrt{\zeta} + 28\zeta^{1/4} \leq 30\zeta^{1/4}. \]

nodes.name: Rerandomizing one coordinate
nodes.statement: For $u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, an index $i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, and $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$, let \[ \operatorname{rerand}_i(u,x) = u + x e_i. \] This is the move obtained by rerandomizing the $i$-th coordinate of $u$ by a uniform additive shift. In Lean, the same edge distribution is represented as the push-forward of the uniform distribution on triples $(u,i,x)$ by the map that replaces the $i$-th coordinate by $x$; since $x$ is uniform, this is the same distribution as the additive-shift presentation. The corresponding weight-sum identity identifies this push-forward distribution with the explicit edge coefficient used in the matrix proof.
nodes.label: def:rerandomize-coord

nodes.name: Hypercube graph
nodes.statement: The hypercube graph $C=(V,E)$ has vertex set $V=\mathbb{F}_q^m$, and an edge between $u$ and $v$ whenever they differ in at most one coordinate. A random edge $(u,v) \sim C$ is sampled by drawing $u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m$, $i \in \{1,\dots,m\}$, and $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$ uniformly and then setting $v=\operatorname{rerand}_i(u,x)$.
nodes.label: def:hypercube-graph

nodes.name: Adjacency matrix and Laplacian
nodes.statement: Let $M=q^m$. The normalized adjacency matrix of $C$ is \[ K = \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \lvert u \rangle\langle v \rvert, \] and the Laplacian is \[ L = \frac{1}{M}I-K. \]
nodes.label: def:adjacency-laplacian

nodes.name: Laplacian rewrite
nodes.statement: The Laplacian can be written as \[ L = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} (\lvert u \rangle-\lvert v \rangle)(\langle u \rvert-\langle v \rvert). \]
nodes.label: prop:laplacian-rewrite

nodes.statement: The two vertex marginals of a random edge are uniform on $\mathbb{F}_q^m$. Expanding the right-hand side yields $(1/M)I-K$.

nodes.name: Average of a nontrivial additive character
nodes.statement: For $\beta \in \mathbb{F}_q$, \[ \mathbb{E}_{x \sim \mathbb{F}_q} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(\beta x)} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \beta=0, \\ 0 & \text{if } \beta\ne 0. \end{cases} \]
nodes.label: lem:character-average-scalar

nodes.statement: If $\beta=0$ the character is constant. If $\beta\ne 0$, the map $x \mapsto \beta x$ permutes $\mathbb{F}_q$, so the average is the average of a nontrivial additive character, which vanishes.

nodes.name: Orthogonality of finite-field characters
nodes.statement: For $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \[ \frac{1}{q^m}\sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot(\beta-\alpha))} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \alpha=\beta, \\ 0 & \text{if } \alpha\ne \beta. \end{cases} \]
nodes.label: lem:character-average-vector

nodes.statement: This is Lemma~\ref{prop:fourier-fact-vector} applied to $v=\beta-\alpha$.

nodes.name: Eigenvectors of the hypercube graph
nodes.statement: For each $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, define \[ \lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \lvert u \rangle. \] Then the following two statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The $\lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle$'s form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^V$. \item For each $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, $\lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle$ is an eigenvector for $K$ with eigenvalue $\frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m}$, where $|\alpha|$ is the number of nonzero coordinates of $\alpha$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: prop:eigenvectors

nodes.statement: First we prove \ref{item:orthonormal}. For $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \[ \langle \varphi_\alpha \mid \varphi_\beta \rangle = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot(\beta-\alpha))} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \alpha=\beta, \\ 0 & \text{if } \alpha\ne \beta, \end{cases} \] by Lemma~\ref{lem:character-average-vector}. Thus the $\lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^V$. Next we prove \ref{item:eigenvector}. For $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} K \cdot \lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle & = \left(\mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \lvert u \rangle\langle v \rvert\right) \cdot \left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \lvert u \rangle\right) \\ & = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(v\cdot \alpha)} \lvert u \rangle. \end{aligned} \end{equation} By the edge-sampling rule from Definition~\ref{def:hypercube-graph}, we may write $v=u+x e_i$, where $i$ is uniformly random in $\{1,\dots,m\}$ and $x$ is uniformly random in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Therefore \[ \eqref{eq:eigenvector-calculation} = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_{u,i,x} \omega^{\operatorname{tr}((u+x e_i)\cdot \alpha)} \lvert u \rangle = \left(\mathbb{E}_{i,x}\omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathbb{E}_u \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(u\cdot \alpha)} \lvert u \rangle = \frac{1}{M}\left(\mathbb{E}_{i,x}\omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right) \cdot \lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle. \] Hence $\lvert \varphi_\alpha \rangle$ is an eigenvector of $K$ with eigenvalue \[ \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathbb{E}_i \left[\mathbb{E}_x \omega^{\operatorname{tr}(x\alpha_i)}\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathbb{E}_i \left[\mathbf{1}\!\left[[\right]\alpha_i=0]\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-|\alpha|}{m}, \] by Lemma~\ref{lem:character-average-scalar}.

nodes.name: Spectral gap of the Laplacian
nodes.statement: If $\lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \le \lambda_{q^m}$ are the eigenvalues of $L$, then \[ \lambda_1=0, \qquad \lambda_2 = \frac{1}{m q^m}. \]
nodes.label: cor:laplacian-spectral-gap

nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{prop:eigenvectors} identifies the two largest eigenvalues of $K$, hence the two smallest eigenvalues of $L=(1/q^m)I-K$.

nodes.name: Local and global variance
nodes.statement: Let $\lvert \psi \rangle \in \mathcal H_{\mathrm A} \otimes \mathcal H_{\mathrm B}$ and let $0 \le A^u \le I$ be an operator for each $u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$. The local variance is \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi) = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u-A^v)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle, \] and the global variance is \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi) = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{u,v\sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u-A^v)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \]
nodes.label: def:local-and-variance

nodes.name: Local variance as a Laplacian form
nodes.statement: Define \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \lvert u \rangle \otimes A^u \otimes I. \] Then \[ \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert) A_{\mathrm{comb}}) = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.label: lem:local-rewrite

nodes.statement: For $u,v \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} ((\langle u \rvert-\langle v \rvert) \otimes \langle \psi \rvert) \cdot A_{\mathrm{comb}} & = ((\langle u \rvert-\langle v \rvert) \otimes \langle \psi \rvert) \cdot \sum_{w \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \lvert w \rangle \otimes A^w \otimes I \\ & = \langle \psi \rvert \cdot ((A^u-A^v)\otimes I). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Therefore \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert) A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger \bigl((\lvert u \rangle-\lvert v \rangle)(\langle u \rvert-\langle v \rvert) \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert\bigr) A_{\mathrm{comb}} \] by Lemma~\ref{prop:laplacian-rewrite}, and hence \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert) A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} ((A^u-A^v)\otimes I)\lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert((A^u-A^v)\otimes I) \] by \eqref{eq:edge-difference-action}. Taking the trace gives \[ \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert) A_{\mathrm{comb}}) = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u-A^v)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi). \]

nodes.name: Global variance as the orthogonal Fourier mass
nodes.statement: Write \[ A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \lvert \varphi_0 \rangle \otimes A_0 + \lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle \otimes A_\perp, \] where $\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle$ is orthogonal to $\lvert \varphi_0 \rangle$. Then \[ \frac{1}{q^m}\mathrm{Tr}((\langle \varphi_\perp \rvert\otimes A_\perp)(I\otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert)(\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp)) = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.label: lem:global-rewrite

nodes.statement: We first compute \[ A_0 = (\langle \varphi_0 \rvert\otimes I)\cdot A_{\mathrm{comb}} = \left(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \langle u \rvert\right) \otimes I \cdot \left(\sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \lvert u \rangle \otimes A^u \otimes I\right) = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} A^u \otimes I. \] Writing $A_{\mathrm{avg}}=\mathbb{E}_u A^u$, it follows that \[ \lvert \varphi_0 \rangle\otimes A_0 = \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \lvert u \rangle \otimes A_{\mathrm{avg}} \otimes I, \qquad \lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp = \sum_{u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m} \lvert u \rangle \otimes (A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \otimes I. \] Hence \begin{equation} \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}((\langle \varphi_\perp \rvert\otimes A_\perp)(I\otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert)(\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp)) = \mathbb{E}_{u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} Moreover, \[ \mathbb{E}_{u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m}(A^u-A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 = \mathbb{E}_{u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m}\bigl((A^u)^2-(A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2\bigr) = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{u,v \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} (A^u-A^v)^2. \] Substituting this identity into \eqref{eq:just-took-trace} yields \[ \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}((\langle \varphi_\perp \rvert\otimes A_\perp)(I\otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert)(\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp)) = \frac12 \mathbb{E}_{u,v \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u-A^v)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi). \]

nodes.name: Local-to-global inequality
nodes.statement: For every family $\{A^u\}$, \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi) \le m\, \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi). \]
nodes.label: lem:local-to-global

nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert) A_{\mathrm{comb}} & = (\langle \varphi_0 \rvert\otimes A_0+\langle \varphi_\perp \rvert\otimes A_\perp)(L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert)(\lvert \varphi_0 \rangle\otimes A_0+\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp) \\ & = (\langle \varphi_\perp \rvert\otimes A_\perp)(L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert)(\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp) \\ & = \langle \varphi_\perp \rvertL\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle \cdot A_\perp \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert A_\perp. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The second step uses that $\lvert \varphi_0 \rangle$ is a $0$-eigenvector of $L$. Since $\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle$ is orthogonal to $\lvert \varphi_0 \rangle$, Lemma~\ref{cor:laplacian-spectral-gap} gives \[ \langle \varphi_\perp \rvertL\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle \ge \frac{1}{mM} \cdot \langle \varphi_\perp \mid \varphi_\perp \rangle. \] Therefore \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi) = \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\mathrm{comb}}^\dagger (L \otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert) A_{\mathrm{comb}}) = \langle \varphi_\perp \rvertL\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle \cdot \mathrm{Tr}(A_\perp \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert A_\perp) \] by Lemma~\ref{lem:local-rewrite} and \eqref{eq:used-0-eigenvector}, so \[ \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi) \ge \frac{1}{mM} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}((\langle \varphi_\perp \rvert\otimes A_\perp)(I\otimes \lvert \psi \rangle\langle \psi \rvert)(\lvert \varphi_\perp \rangle\otimes A_\perp)) = \frac{1}{m}\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi), \] where the last step is Lemma~\ref{lem:global-rewrite}. Rearranging gives the claim.

nodes.name: Replacing a line answer by a fixed polynomial
nodes.statement: Let $G \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$. On the axis-parallel line-test distribution, \[ B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=g(u)]} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{md/q} B^{\ell}_{g|_{\ell}} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}. \]
nodes.section: 6 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.label: lem:generalize-b

nodes.statement: Expand the $\approx_{md/q}$ norm on the weighted vector $(I\otimes (G_g)^{1/2})\lvert \psi \rangle$. Because $B^\ell$ is a projective measurement, only those line polynomials $f$ with $f\ne g|_\ell$ and $f(u)=g(u)$ contribute. Lemma~\ref{lem:axis-line-polynomial-agreement-mdq} is the univariate Schwartz--Zippel wrapper used in Lean for this line-restriction event; it supplies the paper's $md/q$ loss, and the remaining operator sum is bounded by the fact that $G$ is a submeasurement.

nodes.name: Conditional variants for the collision-residual estimate
nodes.statement: The paper proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:generalize-b} bounds the collision event directly by the Schwartz--Zippel estimate. The following conditional variants instead assume this collision estimate, or one of the reindexing identities that implies it, as an explicit hypothesis. These conditional statements make explicit the intermediate estimates still needed for this route; they are not additional hypotheses in the paper statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:generalize-b}.

nodes.label: rem:generalize-b-collision-residual-conditional

nodes.name: Local variance of the points measurements
nodes.statement: Let $G \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$. On the hypercube edge distribution $(u,v) \sim C$, \begin{equation} A^u_{g(u)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{24\cdot\left(\varepsilon+\delta+\frac{md}{q}\right)} A^v_{g(v)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.label: lem:local-variance-of-points

nodes.statement: Fix $g$ and keep the weight $(G_g)^{1/2}$ on the second tensor factor throughout. On the vector $(I\otimes (G_g)^{1/2})\lvert \psi \rangle$ one has the six-step chain \[ A^u_{g(u)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{2\delta} I\otimes (G_g)^{1/2} A^u_{g(u)} \approx_{2\varepsilon} B^\ell_{[f(u)=g(u)]} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{md/q} B^\ell_{g|_\ell} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{md/q} B^\ell_{[f(v)=g(v)]} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{2\varepsilon} I\otimes (G_g)^{1/2} A^v_{g(v)} \approx_{2\delta} A^v_{g(v)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}. \] The first, second, fifth, and sixth comparisons use Lemma~\ref{prop:simeq-to-approx} together with Theorem~\ref{prop:cab-approx-delta} and the good-strategy hypotheses, and the middle pair is Lemma~\ref{lem:generalize-b}. Lemma~\ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta} sums these six weighted transports.

nodes.name: Equivalent local-variance bound
nodes.statement: The local-variance bound for the point measurements is \begin{equation} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)})^2 \otimes G_g \lvert \psi \rangle \le 24\left(\varepsilon+\delta+\frac{md}{q}\right). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.label: lem:equivalent-local-variance

nodes.statement: This is the squared-norm expansion of Lemma~\ref{lem:local-variance-of-points} after summing over the polynomial outcome~$g$. The Lean proof expands the weighted operator difference, telescopes the six transports in the local variance proof, sums the resulting bounds over~$g$, and absorbs the transport-chain error into $24\left(\varepsilon+\delta+\frac{md}{q}\right)$.
nodes.section: 6 Global variance of the points measurements

nodes.name: Polynomial-sum formalization for \ref{eq:equivalent-local-variance}
nodes.statement: The three referenced declarations and Lemma~\ref{lem:equivalent-local-variance} together provide the full polynomial-sum (cardinality-free) chain proving the equation. The chain assembly lemma \texttt{localVarianceDeviation\_sum\_le\_localVarianceOfPointsError} telescopes the six operator differences via \texttt{ev\_sum\_conjTranspose\_mul\_sum\_le}, sums over~$g$, and applies the six individual \texttt{\_sum} bounds (including the reverse~\texttt{generalizeB} sum) to avoid the per-polynomial cardinality blow-up.

nodes.name: Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.statement: Let $G \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$. On the uniform distribution over independent $u,v \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \begin{equation} A^u_{g(u)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \approx_{24m\left(\varepsilon+\delta+\frac{md}{q}\right)} A^v_{g(v)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 6 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.label: lem:global-variance-of-points

nodes.statement: We want to bound \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_{u,v \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} \lVert (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)}) \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \lvert \psi \rangle \rVert^2 = \mathbb{E}_{u,v \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)})^2 \otimes G_g \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} For each $g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)$, define \[ A(g)^u := A^u_{g(u)}, \qquad \lvert \psi_g \rangle := (I \otimes (G_g)^{1/2})\lvert \psi \rangle. \] Then \[ \eqref{eq:global-variance-target} = \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} \mathbb{E}_{u,v \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} \langle \psi_g \rvert (A(g)^u-A(g)^v)^2 \otimes I \lvert \psi_g \rangle = \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} 2\,\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A(g),\psi_g). \] Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:local-to-global} gives \[ \eqref{eq:global-variance-target} \le \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} 2m\,\mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A(g),\psi_g) = m \cdot \sum_{g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)} \mathbb{E}_{(u,v)\sim C} \langle \psi \rvert (A^u_{g(u)}-A^v_{g(v)})^2 \otimes G_g \lvert \psi \rangle. \] The last quantity is at most $m \cdot 24\left(\varepsilon+\delta+\frac{md}{q}\right)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:equivalent-local-variance}, which is exactly \ref{eq:global-variance-of-points-equation}.
nodes.section: 6 Global variance of the points measurements

nodes.name: Self-improvement with non-projective output
nodes.statement: Let $G \in \mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d)$ be a measurement with the following property: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^{m}$, \[ A^{u}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G_{[g(u)=a]}. \] \end{enumerate} Let \[ \zeta = 100m\cdot \Big(\varepsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big). \] Then there exists $H \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Completeness): If $H = \sum_h H_h$, then \[ \langle \psi \rvert H \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq (1-\nu)-\zeta. \] \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \[ A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes H_{[h(u) = a]}. \] \item (Strong self-consistency): \[ \sum_{h} \langle \psi \rvert H_h \otimes H_h \lvert \psi \rangle \geq \langle \psi \rvert H \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \zeta. \] \item (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z$ such that \[ \langle \psi \rvert Z \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle -\mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert A^{u}_{a} \otimes H_{[h(u)=a]} \lvert \psi \rangle \leq \zeta \] and for each $h \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)$, \[ Z \geq \left(\mathbb{E}_{u} A^{u}_{h(u)}\right). \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:self-improvement-helper

nodes.statement: Let $T=\{T_g\}$ and $Z$ be the optimal solutions to the SDPs~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} and~\eqref{eq:dual-objective} given by Lemma~\ref{lem:sdp}. Then $T$ is a measurement, and \begin{align} \forall g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d): \qquad Z &\geq \left(\mathbb{E}_{u} A^{u}_{g(u)}\right), \\ T_g \cdot Z &= T_g \cdot \left(\mathbb{E}_{u} A^{u}_{g(u)}\right). \end{align} For each $u \in \mathbb{F}_q^m$, define $H^u=\{H_h^u\}_{h \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)}$ by \[ H_h^u := A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)}, \] and let \[ H_h := \mathbb{E}_{u} H_h^u. \] The pointwise family $H^u$ is a submeasurement because \[ \sum_h H_h^u = \sum_a A_a^u \cdot \Big(\sum_{h:h(u)=a} T_h\Big)\cdot A_a^u \le \sum_a (A_a^u)^2 = I, \] where the inequality uses that~$T$ is a measurement and the last identity uses that~$A$ is projective. Averaging over~$u$ gives \[ \sum_h H_h = \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_h H_h^u \le I, \] so $H$ is also a submeasurement and therefore lies in~$\mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$. Set \[ \zeta_{\mathrm{variance}} = 24m\cdot\Big(\varepsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big). \] Lemma~\ref{lem:add-in-u} below is the technical transfer from the averaged family~$H$ back to the sandwiched operators $A^u_{h(u)}T_hA^u_{h(u)}$. We use it in the completeness, consistency, strong self-consistency, and boundedness estimates that follow. We now verify the four conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement-helper}. \emph{Proof of \ref{item:self-improvement-completeness}.} The completeness of~$H$ is \begin{align} \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert H_h \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle &= \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert H^{u}_h \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \notag\\ &= \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert \bigl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)}\bigr) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{align} Grouping the polynomials according to their value at~$u$ gives \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert \bigl(A^{u}_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{u}_{h(u)}\bigr) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert \bigl(A^{u}_{a} \cdot T_{[h(u) = a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a}\bigr) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} We first move the leftmost copy of~$A^u_a$ across the bipartition: \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:group-by-point-value} \approx_{2\sqrt{\delta}} \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert \bigl(T_{[h(u)=a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a}\bigr) \otimes A^{u}_{a} \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} The difference is bounded by Cauchy--Schwarz as in~\eqref{eq:move-first-point-projector-cauchy-schwarz}; the first factor is at most $\sqrt{2\delta}$ by self-consistency of~$A$, and the second is at most~$1$ because $T_{[h(u)=a]} \le I$. We next remove the remaining copy of~$A^u_a$ on Bob's side: \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:first-point-projector-transport} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert \bigl(T_{[h(u)=a]} \cdot A^{u}_{a}\bigr) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \end{equation} The first Cauchy--Schwarz factor is at most~$1$ because the fiber operators form a submeasurement after grouping~$T$ by the value of~$h(u)$. Here the second Cauchy--Schwarz factor is \[ \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_{a\neq b} \langle \psi \rvert A^u_a \otimes A^u_b \lvert \psi \rangle, \] which is at most~$\delta$ because~$A$ is self-consistent and projective. Reindexing by~$h$ and using~\eqref{eq:swap-Z-for-A}, \[ \eqref{eq:first-moved-completeness} = \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert \bigl(T_h \cdot \mathbb{E}_{u} A^u_{h(u)}\bigr) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert (T_h \cdot Z) \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle = \langle \psi \rvert Z \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle. \] Thus \begin{equation} \sum_h \langle \psi \rvert H_h \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq \langle \psi \rvert Z \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - 3\sqrt{\delta}. \end{equation} Since $G$ is a measurement,~\eqref{eq:Z-greater-than-A} and Lemma~\ref{prop:simeq-for-measurements} give \[ \langle \psi \rvert Z \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \ge \mathbb{E}_{u} \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert

nodes.name: Uniform SDP feasible witness
nodes.statement: The uniform primal family \(T_g=(2|\mathcal{P}(m,q,d)|)^{-1}I\) has total mass \((1/2)I\), and the dual operator \(Z=2I\) is positive semidefinite and dominates the identity.
nodes.label: lem:sdp-uniform-feasible-witness

nodes.statement: This is the elementary Slater-type feasible witness recorded in the basic self-improvement definitions.

nodes.name: Explicit matrix feasible bounds
nodes.statement: In every concrete matrix realization, the uniform family \(T_g=(2|\mathcal{P}(m,q,d)|)^{-1}I\) has total mass \((1/2)I\). The dual operator \(Z=2I\) dominates the identity and satisfies \(Z-A_g\geq I\), hence \(Z\geq A_g\), for every polynomial \(g\). In the canonical block SDP, the corresponding block matrix is feasible, its slack block is \((1/2)I\), and the canonical dual slack for the same dual witness also dominates the block identity. More generally, dual feasibility implies positivity of \(Z\), since the averaged point operators \(A_g\) are positive semidefinite.
nodes.label: lem:sdp-matrix-feasible-bounds

nodes.statement: The formal proof is the matrix specialization of the uniform SDP witness recorded in the basic definitions. The inequality \(A_g\leq I\) follows by averaging the point-measurement effects and using the submeasurement bound at each point.

nodes.name: Matrix slackness output
nodes.statement: From a matrix-level strong-duality witness with complementary slackness of the shape asserted by Lemma~\ref{lem:sdp}, one obtains a complete measurement \(\{T_g\}\), a feasible dual operator \(Z\), equality of the primal and dual objectives, and the equations \(T_gZ=T_gA_g\) for all \(g\). Lean isolates the saturated canonical optimal-pair output required from strong duality: a feasible canonical primal matrix, a dual-feasible operator with equal objective value, canonical complementary slackness, and vanishing of the extra canonical slack block. This datum gives the matrix-level slackness-carrying SDP statement, whose witness is already a complete matrix measurement, and is then transported to the abstract Section~9 statement without assuming \(I \le Z\). The displayed measurement witness is read directly from that abstract statement. The canonical saturation datum is now the only matrix-level input used to pass from strong duality to the abstract SDP statement. The paper-facing self-improvement helper consumes the resulting abstract SDP statement.
nodes.label: lem:sdp-matrix-slackness-output

nodes.statement: The identity \(\sum_gT_g=I\) turns the optimal primal submeasurement into a measurement; Lean performs this completion before storing the matrix and abstract slackness statements. nodes.name: Dual SDP and complementary slackness
nodes.statement: Let \[ A_g = \mathbb{E}_{u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m} A^u_{g(u)}. \] Then the primal is \begin{align} \sup &\quad \sum_g \,\mathrm{Tr}(T_g \cdot A_g) \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad T_g \geq 0\qquad\forall g\in\mathcal{P}(m,q,d), \notag\\ &\quad \sum_g T_g \leq I, \notag \end{align} and the dual is \begin{align} \inf &\quad \mathrm{Tr}(Z) \\ \text{ s.t.} &\quad Z \geq A_g. \end{align} These semidefinite programs are dual to each other. Moreover there is an optimal pair of solutions $\{T_g\}$ to~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} and $Z$ to~\eqref{eq:dual-objective} such that $\sum_g T_g = I$ and \begin{equation} T_g Z \,=\, T_g {A_g},\qquad\forall g\in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d). \end{equation}
nodes.label: lem:sdp

nodes.statement: Rewrite~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} in canonical block form. Let $r$ be the dimension of the space on which~$A$ acts, let $M = |\mathcal{P}(m,q,d)|$, and fix an ordering $g_1,\ldots,g_M$ of the polynomials. Consider \begin{align} \sup &\quad \mathrm{Tr}(C^\dagger X) \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad \mathrm{Tr}(D_{ij}^\dagger X) = b_{ij} \qquad\forall i,j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}, \notag\\ &\quad X \geq 0, \notag \end{align} where \[ C = \sum_{i = 1}^M \lvert i \rangle\langle i \rvert \otimes A_{g_i}, \] and, for $i,j \in \{1,\ldots,r\}$, \[ D_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \lvert k \rangle\langle k \rvert \otimes \lvert i \rangle\langle j \rvert, \qquad b_{ij} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } i = j,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \] Writing $X=\sum_{i,j=1}^{M+1}\lvert i \rangle\langle j \rvert\otimes X_{ij}$, the constraints say precisely that $\sum_{i=1}^{M+1} X_{ii}=I$, hence $\sum_{i=1}^{M}X_{ii}\le I$, and the objective is \[ \mathrm{Tr}(C^\dagger X)=\sum_{i=1}^M \mathrm{Tr}(A_{g_i}\cdot X_{ii}). \] Thus~\eqref{eq:primal-canonical} is equivalent to~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} under the identification $T_{g_i}=X_{ii}$. The canonical dual is \begin{align} \inf &\quad \sum_i\, z_{ij} b_{ij} \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} \geq C. \end{align} Since \[ \sum_{i,j=1}^r z_{ij} D_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \lvert k \rangle\langle k \rvert \otimes \left(\sum_{i,j=1}^r z_{ij}\lvert i \rangle\langle j \rvert\right) =: \sum_{k=1}^{M+1}\lvert k \rangle\langle k \rvert \otimes Z, \] the constraint~\eqref{eq:dual-canonical-constraint} is exactly $Z\ge A_{g_i}$ for every $i$, and the objective is $\mathrm{Tr}(Z)$. In Lean, the latter statement is recorded as the trace-pairing identity \[ \Re\mathrm{Tr}(D(Z)X)=\Re\mathrm{Tr}(Z) \] for every feasible canonical primal matrix \(X\), where \(D(Z)\) denotes the block-diagonal canonical dual operator. Consequently the canonical primal-dual gap is the real trace pairing of \(X\) with the canonical dual slack \(D(Z)-C\). Since the real trace pairing of positive semidefinite operators is nonnegative, Lean also records the resulting weak-duality inequality for any feasible canonical primal and dual pair. Hence~\eqref{eq:dual-canonical} is equivalent to~\eqref{eq:dual-objective}. Slater's condition holds because \[ T_g = \frac{1}{2M}\cdot I \qquad\forall g\in\mathcal{P}(m,q,d), \qquad Z = 2I \] are strictly feasible for the primal and dual respectively. Therefore strong duality holds. For an optimal pair $(X,(z_{ij}))$ in canonical form, complementary slackness gives \begin{equation} X\Big( \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} - C \Big) \,=\, 0. \end{equation} We may assume that $X$ is block diagonal. Translating~\eqref{eq:complementary-slackness} back to the variables $\{T_g\}$ and~$Z$ yields $T_g(Z-A_g)=0$ for every~$g$ and \(S Z=0\), where \(S=I-\sum_gT_g\) is the slack block. The paper then treats this as forcing \(S=0\). The Lean development records this saturation as part of the canonical optimal-pair datum for the block SDP. The canonical calculation still uses the auxiliary expression \texttt{matrixSdpComplementarySlacknessDefect} to read off the polynomial blocks of \eqref{eq:complementary-slackness}. The matrix optimal-witness interface, however, stores the displayed equation \(T_gZ=T_gA_g\) directly; \texttt{MatrixSdpOptimalWitness.primalMeasurement} expresses \(\sum_g T_g=I\) as a complete measurement. The statement \texttt{MatrixSdpStatementWithSlackness} records this matrix-level strong-duality output and the abstract theorem \texttt{sdp\_statement\_with\_slackness} specializes it to the paper's self-improvement setting. The explicit Slater witnesses used above are isolated in Lemma~\ref{lem:sdp-matrix-feasible-bounds} and separately recorded by \texttt{matrixSdpStrictPrimalSubmeasurement}, \texttt{matrixSdpStrictDualWitness}, and \texttt{matrixSdpFeasibleBounds\_canonical}; the dual feasibility of \(2I\) follows from \texttt{matrixAveragedPointOperator\_le\_one}. nodes.name: Auxiliary self-improvement lemmas
nodes.statement: Several auxiliary results are used to prove Theorem~\ref{thm:self-improvement} from the helper output and the orthonormalization theorem. They record local intermediate estimates and final-field assembly lemmas. The former orthonormalization spectral-transport record has been retired; the spectral-truncation part of the construction is now represented directly by \texttt{spectralTruncationStatement\_of\_sourceAlmostProjective}. This result is not a locality-preserving repair theorem. The theorem below records the paper-facing conclusion. Its proof follows the expectation-level completeness argument from the paper; the obstruction to a generic operator-total strengthening is recorded in issue~\#1642.
nodes.label: rem:self-improvement-lean-interfaces

nodes.name: Self-improvement
nodes.statement: Let $G \in \mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d)$ be a measurement with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^{m}$, \[ A^{u}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G_{[g(u)=a]}. \] \end{enumerate} Let \[ \zeta = 3000m\cdot \Big(\varepsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big). \] Then there exists a projective submeasurement $H \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Completeness): If $H = \sum_h H_h$, then \[ \langle \psi \rvert H \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq (1-\nu)-\zeta. \] \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \[ A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes H_{[h(u) = a]}. \] \item (Strong self-consistency): \[ H_h \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes H_h. \] \item (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z$ such that \[ \langle \psi \rvert Z \otimes (I - H) \lvert \psi \rangle \leq \zeta \] and for each $h \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)$, \[ Z \geq \left(\mathbb{E}_{u} A^{u}_{h(u)}\right). \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: thm:self-improvement

nodes.statement: The bound is trivial if one of $\varepsilon$, $\delta$, or $d/q$ is at least~$1$, so assume all three are at most~$1$. In Lean, the third assumption is recorded as $d \le q$, which is equivalent to $d/q \le 1$ since $q>0$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement-helper} to~$G$ and let $\widehat H \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$ be the output, with \[ \widehat{\zeta} = 100m \cdot \Big(\varepsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big). \] By \ref{item:self-improvement-self} of Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement-helper}, \[ \sum_{h} \langle \psi \rvert \widehat{H}_h \otimes \widehat{H}_h \lvert \psi \rangle \geq \langle \psi \rvert \widehat{H} \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \widehat{\zeta}. \] Therefore Theorem~\ref{thm:orthonormalization} supplies a projective submeasurement $H \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$ such that \begin{equation} \widehat{H}_h \otimes I \approx_{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} H_{h} \otimes I, \end{equation} where \[ \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}} = 100 \widehat{\zeta}^{1/4}. \] In addition, Lemma~\ref{prop:self-consistency-implies-data-processing} implies that \begin{equation} \widehat{H}_{[h(u)=a]} \otimes I \approx_{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}} H_{[h(u)=a]} \otimes I, \end{equation} where \[ \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}} = 8 \widehat{\zeta} + 8 \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}. \] The four conclusions are transferred one by one. \emph{Proof of \ref{item:self-improvement-projective-completeness}.} Lemma~\ref{prop:completeness-transfer-self-consistent-A} implies \[ \langle \psi \rvert H \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \geq \langle \psi \rvert \widehat{H} \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \widehat{\zeta} - 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} \geq (1-\nu) - 2\widehat{\zeta} - 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}, \] where the second inequality is \ref{item:self-improvement-completeness} of Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement-helper}. \emph{Proof of \ref{item:self-improvement-projective-A-consistency}.} Lemma~\ref{prop:triangle-sub} applied to \ref{item:self-improvement-A-consistency} of Lemma~\ref{lem:self-improvement-helper} and the post-processed comparison~\eqref{eq:approx-data-processed} gives \[ A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\widehat{\zeta} + \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}}} I \otimes H_{[h(u) = a]}. \] In Lean the corresponding transport is stated for submeasurements with the total-overlap displacement recorded explicitly; this is the term which vanishes in the measurement-valued form of Lemma~\ref{prop:triangle-sub}. The monotone-total route records a sufficient structural replacement: if the orthonormalization repair preserves the completed residual outcome, then the projective total is bounded by the helper total as an operator, hence also has no larger right-register expectation in the strategy state. Under this structural hypothesis the alphabet-size displacement term is not introduced. At present the formal QXP algebra only isolates the construction-level statement \(Q_{\mathrm{none}} \leq P_{\mathrm{none}}\), obtained when the repair preserves the fresh row block \(\widehat X_{\mathrm{none}}=X_{\mathrm{none}}\). The former generic ``RestrictSome'' monotone-total route would have required one to turn this into the source-facing inequality \(\widehat A_{\bot} \leq \widehat P_{\bot}\), by adding a comparison between the completed source residual and the ``Q''-layer fresh outcome. The present formal development no longer uses that generic route, and the comparison is false without additional hypotheses; see \texttt{docs/reports/issue-1642-restrictsome-residual-domination-obstruction.md}. nodes.name: Shared diagonal-line sample
nodes.statement: Sample a uniformly random ordered point pair $(u,v)$ and a uniformly random parameter $t \in \mathbb{F}_q$. Package this data as the diagonal line whose direction is $v-u$ and whose parametrization visits $u$ at $t$ and $v$ at $t+1$.

nodes.name: Commutativity of the point measurements
nodes.statement: Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\varepsilon,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m,q,d)$ low individual degree test. On average over independent and uniformly random $u,v \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m$, \[ (A_a^u A_b^v) \otimes I \approx_{32\gamma m} (A_b^v A_a^u) \otimes I. \]
nodes.label: thm:commutativity-points

nodes.statement: By Definition~\ref{def:restricted-diagonal-lines-test}, the strategy passes the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma m$. Hence \[ A_a^u \otimes I \simeq_{\gamma m} I \otimes L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]} \] on average over uniformly random $u \sim \mathbb{F}_q^m$ and a uniformly random line $\ell$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^m$ containing $u$. By \ref{prop:simeq-to-approx}, \begin{equation} A_a^u \otimes I \approx_{2\gamma m} I \otimes L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]}. \end{equation} Let $u$ and $v$ be independent uniformly random points in $\mathbb{F}_q^m$, and let $\ell$ be a uniformly random line containing both points. The marginal distribution on $(u,\ell)$ and on $(v,\ell)$ is the same as above, so \begin{align*} (A_a^u A_b^v) \otimes I & \approx_{2\gamma m} A_a^u \otimes L^\ell_{[f(v)=b]} \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \\ & \approx_{2\gamma m} I \otimes \bigl(L^\ell_{[f(v)=b]} L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]}\bigr) \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \\ & = I \otimes \bigl(L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]} L^\ell_{[f(v)=b]}\bigr) \tag{because~$L$ is projective} \\ & \approx_{2\gamma m} A_b^v \otimes L^\ell_{[f(u)=a]} \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \\ & \approx_{2\gamma m} (A_b^v A_a^u) \otimes I. \tag{by \ref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \end{align*} The theorem follows from \ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.

nodes.name: Commutativity of~$G$ after evaluation
nodes.statement: Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\varepsilon,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ low individual degree test. Let $\{G^x\} \in \mathrm{PolySub}(m,q,d)$ be a collection of projective sub-measurements indexed by $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$) On average over $(u,x) \sim \mathbb{F}_q^{m+1}$, \[ A_a^{u,x} \otimes I \simeq_\zeta I \otimes G^x_{[g(u)=a]}. \] \item (Strong self-consistency) On average over $x \sim \mathbb{F}_q$, \[ G_g^x \otimes I \approx_\zeta I \otimes G_g^x. \] \item (Boundedness) There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix $Z^x$ for each $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_x \langle \psi \rvert (I-G^x) \otimes Z^x \lvert \psi \rangle \le \zeta \] and for each $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$ and $g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)$, \[ Z^x \ge \left(\mathbb{E}_u A_{g(u)}^{u,x}\right). \] \end{enumerate} Let \[ \nu = 48m\bigl(\gamma^{1/2}+\zeta^{1/2}\bigr). \] Then on average over independent and uniformly random $(u,x),(v,y) \sim \mathbb{F}_q^{m+1}$, \[ G^x_{[g(u)=a]} G^y_{[h(v)=b]} \otimes I \approx_\nu G^y_{[h(v)=b]} G^x_{[g(u)=a]} \otimes I. \]

nodes.name: Distinct tuples
nodes.statement: For $k \ge 1$, let $\mathsf{Distinct}_k \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^k$ be the set of tuples $(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ with pairwise distinct coordinates.
nodes.label: def:distinct-tuples

nodes.name: Distinct tuples versus independent tuples
nodes.statement: If $x=(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ is uniformly random in $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ and $y=(y_1,\dots,y_k)$ is uniformly random in $\mathsf{Distinct}_k$, then \[ d_{\mathrm{TV}}(x,y) \le \frac{k^2}{q}. \]
nodes.label: prop:ld-dnoteq

nodes.statement: The total variation distance is exactly the probability mass of the collision event for a uniformly random tuple, because the distinct-tuple distribution is the uniform distribution conditioned on landing in $\mathsf{Distinct}_k$. A uniformly random tuple lies outside $\mathsf{Distinct}_k$ only if two coordinates collide, so a union bound gives \[ \Pr[x \notin \mathsf{Distinct}_k] \le \sum_{i=2}^k \frac{i-1}{q} = \frac{k(k-1)}{2q}\le \frac{k^2}{q}, \] and this bounds the total variation distance.

Equivalently, \[ \langle \psi \rvert G \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \langle \psi \rvert G^{d+1} \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle \le 2\cdot \Delta^{1/(d+1)}. \] For constant~$d$, this is exactly the heuristic completeness comparison for the first construction recorded in `references/ldt-paper/ld-pasting.tex`.

nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:looks-easy-but-took-me-a-while} pointwise to the spectral distribution of \(G\), and then use the concavity of \(a \mapsto a^{1/(d+1)}\). The displayed operator expression is the same quantity written in the eigenbasis of \(G\).

nodes.name: The incomplete part and the completed measurement
nodes.statement: For each $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$, write $G^x = \sum_g G_g^x$ and define the incomplete outcome $G_\bot^x = I-G^x$. The completed measurement $\widehat G^x$ has outcome set $\mathcal{P}(m,q,d) \cup \{\bot\}$ and is given by \[ \widehat G_g^x = G_g^x \quad (g \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)), \qquad \widehat G_\bot^x = G_\bot^x. \]
nodes.label: def:G-hat

nodes.name: Types
nodes.statement: A type is a vector $\tau \in \{0,1\}^k$. Its weight $|\tau|$ records how many coordinates lie in $\mathcal{P}(m,q,d)$ rather than equal $\bot$.
nodes.label: def:types

nodes.name: The pasted measurement
nodes.statement: Fix $k \ge d+1$. For $x_1,\dots,x_k \in \mathbb{F}_q$ and outcomes $g_1,\dots,g_k \in \mathcal{P}(m,q,d)\cup\{\bot\}$, define \[ \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{x_1,\dots,x_k} = \widehat G_{g_1}^{x_1}\widehat G_{g_2}^{x_2}\cdots \widehat G_{g_k}^{x_k}\cdots \widehat G_{g_2}^{x_2}\widehat G_{g_1}^{x_1}. \] If $(x_1,\dots,x_k)\in \mathsf{Distinct}_k$ and $h \in \mathcal{P}(m+1,q,d)$, define \[ H_h^{x_1,\dots,x_k} = \sum_{\tau:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} \widehat H_{h_\tau}^{x_1,\dots,x_k}, \] where the tuple $h_\tau$ has $i$-th entry $h|_{x_i}$ when $\tau_i=1$ and $\bot$ when $\tau_i=0$. The pasted submeasurement is then \[ H_h = \mathbb{E}_{(x_1,\dots,x_k)\sim \mathsf{Distinct}_k} H_h^{x_1,\dots,x_k}. \]
nodes.label: def:pasted-measurement

nodes.name: Completed-outcome reindexing
nodes.statement: The completed outcome tuples admit the reindexings obtained by separating the first coordinate, moving a third slice to the front, and identifying the one-coordinate split with the original slice question and outcome spaces.
nodes.label: def:completed-outcome-reindexing

nodes.name: Vertical restriction identities
nodes.statement: Restricting an interpolated polynomial to a vertical line and then postprocessing at a point agrees with evaluating the corresponding slice. The same identities commute with averaging over indexed submeasurements.
nodes.label: lem:vertical-restriction-identities

nodes.statement: The compatibility calculation for the restriction and evaluation maps used in the construction of~$H$ expands the vertical restriction, the interpolation support condition, postprocessing, and averaging over indexed submeasurements.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency of the complete part
nodes.statement: In the nontrivial-regime pasting context of Definition~\ref{def:ld-pasting-context}, \[ G^x \otimes I \approx_\zeta I \otimes G^x. \]
nodes.label: lem:g-complete-self-consistency

nodes.statement: Because $G$ is projective, \ref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency} identifies the assumed strong self-consistency of the outcome-level family with \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_x \sum_g \langle \psi \rvert G_g^x \otimes G_g^x \lvert \psi \rangle \ge \mathbb{E}_x \sum_g \langle \psi \rvert G_g^x \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - \frac{\zeta}{2}. \end{equation} Hence \begin{align*} & \mathbb{E}_x \|(G^x\otimes I - I\otimes G^x)\lvert \psi \rangle\|^2 \\ ={} & 2\mathbb{E}_x \langle \psi \rvert G^x \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - 2\mathbb{E}_x \langle \psi \rvert G^x \otimes G^x \lvert \psi \rangle \\ ={} & 2\mathbb{E}_x \sum_g \langle \psi \rvert G_g^x \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - 2\mathbb{E}_x \sum_{g,h} \langle \psi \rvert G_g^x \otimes G_h^x \lvert \psi \rangle \\ \le{} & 2\mathbb{E}_x \sum_g \langle \psi \rvert G_g^x \otimes I \lvert \psi \rangle - 2\mathbb{E}_x \sum_g \langle \psi \rvert G_g^x \otimes G_g^x \lvert \psi \rangle \le \zeta \end{align*} by \ref{eq:ld-g-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency of the incomplete part
nodes.statement: In the nontrivial-regime pasting context of Definition~\ref{def:ld-pasting-context}, \[ G_\bot^x \otimes I \approx_\zeta I \otimes G_\bot^x. \]
nodes.label: cor:g-bot-self-consistency

nodes.statement: Since $G_\bot^x = I-G^x$, \[ G_\bot^x \otimes I - I \otimes G_\bot^x = I \otimes G^x - G^x \otimes I, \] so the claim is immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem:g-complete-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Switcheroo contraction estimates
nodes.statement: After one commutation of a $G$-factor through an auxiliary projective family, the two fourth-term contractions are bounded by the same self-consistency and commutation errors used in the switcheroo argument.
nodes.label: lem:switcheroo-contraction-estimates

nodes.statement: After expanding the fourth switcheroo term, the inserted complete part forms a positive contraction. The left and right Cauchy--Schwarz side conditions are therefore the corresponding sums of $X_gX_g^\ast$ and $X_g^\ast X_g$, where $X_g=\sum_o G_{\bot}^x M_o^yG_g^xM_o^y$. Orthogonality of the projective slice family and the submeasurement inequalities for $M$ and $G_{\bot}$ bound both sums by the identity. These are precisely the two contraction witnesses used in the fourth-term switcheroo chain.

nodes.statement: In the nontrivial-regime pasting context of Definition~\ref{def:ld-pasting-context}, \[ G_g^x G_\bot^y \otimes I \approx_{\nu_2} G_\bot^y G_g^x \otimes I, \qquad G_\bot^x G_\bot^y \otimes I \approx_{\nu_2} G_\bot^y G_\bot^x \otimes I. \]

nodes.statement: The completed measurements $\widehat G^x$ satisfy \begin{align} \widehat G_g^x \otimes I & \approx_{2\zeta} I \otimes \widehat G_g^x, \\ \widehat G_g^x \widehat G_h^y \otimes I & \approx_{\nu_3} \widehat G_h^y \widehat G_g^x \otimes I, \end{align} where \[ \nu_3 = 138m\left(\gamma^{1/16}+\zeta^{1/16}+(d/q)^{1/16}\right). \]

nodes.name: Completed part bounded by a slice
nodes.statement: For every $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$, the squared-distance defect of the one-outcome complete part is bounded by that of the original slice submeasurement: \[ \bigl\| (G^x \otimes I - I \otimes G^x)\lvert \psi \rangle \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; \sum_g \bigl\| (G^x_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^x_g)\lvert \psi \rangle \bigr\|^2, \] where $G^x = \sum_g G^x_g$ is the total operator of the slice submeasurement.
nodes.label: lem:q-sdd-complete-part-slice-bound

nodes.statement: This is the monotonicity estimate for the completed part of~$\widehat G$: the completed contribution is one summand of the corresponding slice squared-distance defect, and the remaining summands are nonnegative.

nodes.name: Completed sandwich normalization
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{Head--tail split identities.} For every $k \ge 0$, point tuple ${\boldsymbol{x}} = (x_1,\dots,x_{k+1})$, and outcome tuple $\boldsymbol{g} = (g_1,\dots,g_{k+1})$, \[ \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1}\cdots \widehat G^{x_{k+1}}_{g_{k+1}} = \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \bigl( \widehat G^{x_2}_{g_2}\cdots \widehat G^{x_{k+1}}_{g_{k+1}} \bigr), \] and the right half-sandwich analogously rotates the head to the tail. \item \textbf{Sum-of-adjoint-products bounds.} For every $r\ge 0$ and ${\boldsymbol{x}} = (x_1,\dots,x_r) \in \mathbb{F}_q^r$, \[ \sum_{g_1,\dots,g_r} \bigl(\widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\bigr)^\dagger \bigl(\widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\bigr) \;\le\; I, \] and the same bound holds for the reverse-order product family. \item \textbf{Generic tensor contraction.} If families~$\{A_a\}_a$ and~$\{B_b\}_b$ satisfy $\sum_a A_a^\dagger A_a \le I$ and $\sum_b B_b^\dagger B_b \le I$, then \[ \sum_{a,b} (A_a \otimes B_b)^\dagger (A_a \otimes B_b) \le I. \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:completed-sandwich-normalization

nodes.statement: The split identities follow from the completed-outcome equivalences. The normalization inequalities are the corresponding submeasurement bounds for the left and right half-products after reindexing the sums.

nodes.name: One-step completed sandwich commutation
nodes.statement: Given the completed-measurement self-consistency and commutation estimates from Corollary~\ref{cor:G-hat-facts}, the following one-step estimates hold. \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{Self-consistency step.} For every~$r\ge 0$, \[ \mathbb{E}_{x,y,z}\mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_r} \sum_{g} \bigl\| \bigl(\widehat G^{z}_g \otimes I - I \otimes \widehat G^{z}_g\bigr) \lvert \psi \rangle \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; 2\zeta. \] \item \textbf{Commutation step.} For every~$r\ge 0$, \[ \mathbb{E}_{x,y}\mathbb{E}_{x_1,\dots,x_r} \sum_{g,h}\sum_{g_1,\dots,g_r} \bigl\| \bigl( \widehat G^{x}_g \widehat G^{y}_h \otimes \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\cdots \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} - \widehat G^{y}_h \widehat G^{x}_g \otimes \widehat G^{x_r}_{g_r}\cdots \widehat G^{x_1}_{g_1} \bigr) \lvert \psi \rangle \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; \nu_3. \] \item \textbf{Two-factor base case.} For $k=2$, the commutation chain reduces to the same tensor-placement convention with the reverse tail product equal to the identity, hence to the pairwise estimate~$\nu_3$. \item \textbf{Split equivalences.} The half-sandwich families are equivalent, under the head--tail reindexing of Lemma~\ref{lem:completed-sandwich-normalization}, to the chain-families used in the move estimates above, with ordered products on the first tensor factor and reverse products on the second tensor factor where these appear in the commutation step. \end{enumerate} These are the elementary building blocks assembled by the recursive chain construction in the following lemma.
nodes.label: lem:one-step-completed-sandwich-commutation

nodes.statement: For the one-step commutation move, rewrite the relevant head--tail split, apply the self-consistency and commutation estimates for~$\widehat G$, and assemble the resulting comparison by the triangle inequality for~$\approx_\delta$.

nodes.name: Commuting past multiple completed measurements
nodes.statement: For every $k \ge 2$, \[ \widehat G_{g_1}^{x_1}\widehat G_{g_2}^{x_2}\cdots \widehat G_{g_k}^{x_k} \otimes I \approx_{\nu_4} \widehat G_{g_2}^{x_2}\cdots \widehat G_{g_k}^{x_k}\widehat G_{g_1}^{x_1} \otimes I, \] where \[ \nu_4 = 426k^2m\left(\gamma^{1/16}+\zeta^{1/16}+(d/q)^{1/16}\right). \]
nodes.label: lem:commute-g-half-sandwich

nodes.statement: Repeatedly move the leftmost factor across the remaining product, using \ref{eq:g-hat-self-consistency} and \ref{eq:g-hat-commutativity} at each step and summing the resulting errors with \ref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}. The paper's calculation gives \[ 3k\bigl(4k\zeta + k\nu_3\bigr) \le 426k^2m\left(\gamma^{1/16}+\zeta^{1/16}+(d/q)^{1/16}\right). \]

nodes.name: Line-interpolation mismatch estimates
nodes.statement: If the tuple of completed slices does not interpolate to the sampled vertical-line value, then some active coordinate witnesses a line-value mismatch. Concretely, for every direction $u$ and injective tuple $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_k)$, let $\widehat{H}^{\mathbf{x}}\rvert_u$ be the vertical-line restriction of the pasted interpolation family. Then \[ \operatorname{Defect}_\psi\bigl( \widehat{H}^{\mathbf{x}}\rvert_u,\, B^u\bigr) \;\le\; \operatorname{Bad}(\psi;u,\mathbf{x}) \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^k \operatorname{Defect}_\psi\bigl( \widehat{H}^{(i)}(u,\mathbf{x}),\, B^{(i)}(u,\mathbf{x})\bigr), \] where $\operatorname{Defect}_\psi(A,B)$ denotes the bipartite consistency defect $\max\bigl(0,\, \langle \psi \rvert A_{\mathrm{tot}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{tot}}\lvert \psi \rangle - \sum_a \langle \psi \rvert A_a\otimes B_a\lvert \psi \rangle\bigr)$, \[ \operatorname{Bad}(\psi;u,\mathbf{x}) = \sum_f \langle \psi \rvert \Bigl(\sum_{\substack{g_1,\dots,g_k\\ \exists i:\, g_i\ne\bot,\ g_i(u)\ne f(x_i)}} \widehat H_{g_1,\dots,g_k}^{\mathbf{x}} \Bigr) \otimes B_f^u \lvert \psi \rangle, \] and $\widehat{H}^{(i)},B^{(i)}$ are the one-point line comparison families (Lemma~\ref{lem:ld-sandwich-line-one-point}) restricted to coordinate $i$, and $\operatorname{Bad}(\psi;u,\mathbf{x})\le 1$.
nodes.label: lem:line-interpolation-mismatch-estimates

nodes.name: Truncated type sums
nodes.statement: For $1 \le \ell \le k+1$ and a tail type $\tau_{\ge \ell} \in \{0,1\}^{k-\ell+1}$, define \[ S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} = \sum_{\tau_{<\ell}\,:\,|\tau|\ge d+1} G^{|\tau_{<\ell}|}(I-G)^{(\ell-1)-|\tau_{<\ell}|}. \] This records the contribution of all prefixes that can still be completed to total weight at least $d+1$ once the tail $\tau_{\ge \ell}$ is fixed.
nodes.label: def:truncated-type-sums

nodes.name: Recurrence for truncated type sums
nodes.statement: Each $S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}$ is Hermitian, positive semidefinite, and bounded by $I$. Moreover, if $\tau_{>\ell}$ is a tail type of length $k-\ell$, then \[ S_{\tau_{>\ell}} = \sum_{\tau_\ell \in \{0,1\}} S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} G^{\tau_\ell}(I-G)^{1-\tau_\ell}. \]
nodes.label: lem:truncated-type-sum-recurrence

nodes.statement: Every summand is a polynomial in the commuting positive operators $G$ and $I-G$, so $S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}}$ is Hermitian and positive semidefinite. Summing over all prefixes gives \[ S_{\tau_{\ge \ell}} \le (G+(I-G))^{\ell-1}=I. \] Splitting the next type bit according to whether $\tau_\ell=1$ or $\tau_\ell=0$ gives the stated recurrence.

nodes.statement: Let $\lvert \psi_{\mathrm{bi}} \rangle$ be a bipartite state on $\iota \otimes \iota$. nodes.name: Appending a line at height $x$
nodes.statement: For $x \in \mathbb{F}_q$, let $\operatorname{append}_x(\ell)$ be the line in $\mathbb{F}_q^{m+1}$ obtained by appending the coordinate $x$ to every point of a line $\ell \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^m$.
